core_obligations: Represent the target (proof lines 11927-11938): choose a quasi-isomorphism F^bullet -> I^bullet into a K-injective complex and let (H')^bullet be the product complex of internal homs SheafHom(O)(E^{-q}, I^p) over n = p + q, which represents R SheafHom(E^bullet, F^bullet) by the construction of the internal-hom section.

Compare the Hom sets (proof lines 11939-11951): the map from Hom_{K(O_U)}(E^bullet|_U, I^bullet|_U) to H^0((H')^bullet(U)) = Hom_{D(O_U)}(E^bullet|_U, I^bullet|_U) is an isomorphism by the local comparison lemma, so the sheafification of U |-> H^0(H^bullet(U)) equals that of U |-> H^0((H')^bullet(U)).
Conclude quasi-isomorphism (proof lines 11952-11956): the same argument applies to the other cohomology sheaves, so H^bullet is quasi-isomorphic to (H')^bullet, which is the assertion.
proof_roadmap: Choose a K-injective resolution of the second complex and write down the product complex representing the derived internal hom.
Use the local comparison lemma to identify the sheafified H^0 of both complexes, and similarly in every degree.
Conclude that the termwise internal hom complex is quasi-isomorphic to the representing complex.
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the derived internal hom of a strictly perfect complex with an arbitrary complex termwise (statement lines 11911-11924). The proof (proof lines 11926-11956) represents the derived internal hom by the product complex attached to a K-injective resolution, compares the two complexes degree by degree through the local comparison lemma identifying their sheafified cohomology, and concludes quasi-isomorphism. H2: one comparison lemma applied degree by degree, written out.
